case_title: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
legal_issue: Standardisation of future prospects and conventional heads in motor accident death compensation under Sections 166/168.
holding_summary: A Constitution Bench held future prospects must be added even for self-employed/fixed-income deceased (40% up to age 40, tapering with age), and fixed uniform amounts for loss of consortium, loss of estate, and funeral expenses.
principle_summary: Resolved a conflict between Reshma Kumari and Rajesh v. Rajbir Singh; is now the binding standard for compensation heads nationwide.

case_title: Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.
legal_issue: Lack of uniformity among Tribunals in choosing the multiplier and deducting personal/living expenses for dependency computation.
holding_summary: Laid down a standard age-banded multiplier table (18 down to 5) and fixed personal-expense deductions at one-third (married) or one-half (unmarried, no dependants).
principle_summary: Foundational multiplier framework; later refined (not overturned) by Pranay Sethi on the future-prospects question.

case_title: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Swaran Singh & Ors.
legal_issue: Scope of an insurers statutory defences under Section 149(2) of the MV Act, particularly regarding an uninsured/improperly licensed driver.
holding_summary: Held the insurers defence is narrow: it must prove a wilful, fundamental breach by the insured (e.g. driver held no licence at all, or a licence for a wholly different class) before it can avoid liability to a third party.
principle_summary: Insurer cannot escape liability for minor or technical licensing defects; protects third-party accident victims as the Acts core social-welfare objective.

case_title: Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr.
legal_issue: Whether the Sarla Verma multiplier table should be treated as a rigid or flexible guideline.
holding_summary: Reaffirmed the Sarla Verma multiplier table as the correct standard, while clarifying some flexibility in exceptional cases.
principle_summary: Cited alongside Sarla Verma as settled law on multiplier selection, until refined further by Pranay Sethi.

case_title: Rajesh & Ors. v. Rajbir Singh & Ors.
legal_issue: Whether future prospects should be added to income for self-employed or fixed-salary (non-permanent) victims.
holding_summary: Held future prospects should be added even for self-employed and fixed-salary victims, creating a conflict with the stricter Sarla Verma position that was later resolved in Pranay Sethi.
principle_summary: Part of the doctrinal lineage (Santosh Devi -> Rajesh -> Pranay Sethi) expanding who qualifies for a future-prospects addition.

case_title: Kaushnuma Begum & Ors. v. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
legal_issue: Whether liability under Section 140/163A (no-fault liability) is fault-based or strict.
holding_summary: Held liability under the no-fault provisions is a form of strict/no-fault liability, akin to liability for use of a dangerous machine, not requiring proof of negligence.
principle_summary: Basis for the summary, no-fault compensation route that runs alongside the fuller Section 166 fault-based claim.

case_title: Deepal Girishbhai Soni & Ors. v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
legal_issue: Whether the structured-formula compensation under Section 163A can be claimed together with a full Section 166 fault-based claim.
holding_summary: Held Section 163A and Section 166 are mutually exclusive alternative remedies; a claimant who opts for the structured formula under 163A cannot also pursue the larger 166 claim.
principle_summary: Clarified the two-track compensation scheme (quick structured-formula route vs. fuller fault-based litigation route) under the MV Act.

case_title: Nagappa v. Gurudayal Singh & Ors.
legal_issue: Whether a Claims Tribunal is restricted to the compensation amount originally claimed in the petition.
holding_summary: Held Tribunals are not bound by the amount claimed and can award just compensation exceeding it if the evidence supports a higher figure.
principle_summary: Reinforces that MACT proceedings are not adversarial litigation capped by pleadings, but aimed at fair, evidence-based compensation.

case_title: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Charlie & Ors.
legal_issue: Whether an insurer can escape liability when the driver held a learners licence at the time of the accident.
holding_summary: Held that if the learners licence holder was driving in accordance with the conditions prescribed (e.g. accompanied by a qualified instructor), the insurer remains liable.
principle_summary: Narrows the improperly licensed driver defence available to insurers under Section 149(2).

case_title: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nicolletta Rohtagi & Ors.
legal_issue: Grounds available to an insurer to resist an award and whether it can raise all defences available to the insured owner.
holding_summary: Held the insurers right to contest is confined strictly to the limited statutory grounds in Section 149(2); it cannot step into the insureds shoes and raise every defence the owner could have raised.
principle_summary: An important early precedent narrowing insurer defences, later refined and partly explained in Swaran Singh.

case_title: Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors.
legal_issue: What standard of proof applies to establishing the manner of an accident in MACT proceedings.
holding_summary: Held MACT proceedings require proof on a preponderance-of-probability standard (as in civil cases), not the stricter beyond-reasonable-doubt standard used in criminal trials, even where a companion criminal case exists.
principle_summary: Frequently cited so that an acquittal or pending criminal case does not automatically defeat a compensation claim.

case_title: Kishan Gopal & Anr. v. Lala & Ors.
legal_issue: Method for computing compensation on the death of a minor child in a motor accident.
holding_summary: Laid down guidance for notional income and multiplier selection specific to child victims, given the absence of any actual earning history.
principle_summary: Fills a gap the general Sarla Verma table does not directly address for very young deceased victims.

case_title: S. Rajaseekaran v. Union of India & Ors.
legal_issue: Continuing mandamus on state and central compliance with road-safety measures (speed governors, helmet enforcement, trauma care, highway engineering defects).
holding_summary: Court has issued a long series of directions to Union and State governments on road-safety implementation, monitored through periodic status reports, rather than a single final disposition.
principle_summary: Example of a live, ongoing case (not a closed precedent) that a legal-answer system must not treat as fully settled; status changes with each order.

case_title: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pushpa & Ors.
legal_issue: Whether the Rajesh v. Rajbir Singh future-prospects rule should extend to all classes of deceased victims.
holding_summary: A two-judge Bench doubted the correctness of extending Rajeshs future-prospects rule uniformly and referred the question to a larger Bench.
principle_summary: This reference is what ultimately produced the Constitution Bench ruling in Pranay Sethi.

case_title: Santosh Devi v. National Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.
legal_issue: Whether future-prospects addition under Susamma Thomas should be limited only to victims with permanent, salaried jobs.
holding_summary: Held the future-prospects principle should not be confined to salaried employees alone and can extend to self-employed and non-permanent workers.
principle_summary: An early step in the doctrinal chain later consolidated in Pranay Sethi.

case_title: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanuram (@ Chuhru Ram) & Ors.
legal_issue: Whether loss of consortium should be limited to a spouse, or extend to parents and children of the deceased.
holding_summary: Held loss of consortium includes spousal, parental, and filial consortium, each separately compensable as a conventional head.
principle_summary: Expanded and clarified the conventional-heads framework set up in Pranay Sethi.

case_title: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Satinder Kaur & Ors.
legal_issue: Multiplier and future-prospects treatment for a self-employed/elderly deceased with limited documentary income proof.
holding_summary: Applied the Pranay Sethi/Sarla Verma framework to a self-employed victim, addressing how to estimate income and multiplier absent formal salary records.
principle_summary: Illustrates application of the standardised framework to informal-sector victims, a common real-world MACT scenario in India.

case_title: Mallikarjun v. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd.
legal_issue: Distinction between functional disability and physical/permanent disability percentage in computing loss of earning capacity.
holding_summary: Held compensation should be based on functional disability (impact on the specific victims occupation and earning capacity), not solely the medical percentage of physical impairment.
principle_summary: Frequently applied in permanent-disability claims to avoid under-compensating victims whose occupation is especially affected by a given injury.

case_title: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr.
legal_issue: What heads of compensation a Tribunal must separately consider in permanent-disability (non-fatal) injury claims.
holding_summary: Laid down a structured checklist of heads (medical expenses, loss of earnings during treatment, loss of future earning capacity, pain and suffering, loss of amenities/marriage prospects, etc.) that Tribunals must address.
principle_summary: A companion framework to Sarla Verma/Pranay Sethi but specific to injury (non-death) claims.

case_title: Manjuri Bera v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Anr.
legal_issue: Whether only legal representatives in the strict succession-law sense can claim compensation under Section 166.
holding_summary: Held the term legal representative in Section 166 must be interpreted broadly and beneficially, not restricted to persons entitled to a share under succession law.
principle_summary: Widens the class of dependants who may bring a compensation claim beyond strict legal heirs.

case_title: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal & Ors.
legal_issue: Whether a married daughter living separately can be treated as a dependant for compensation purposes.
holding_summary: Held dependency must be assessed on actual facts of financial dependence, not presumed absent or present merely from marital/residential status.
principle_summary: Fact-sensitive precedent frequently cited in disputes over who qualifies as a dependant claimant.

case_title: Helen C. Rebello & Ors. v. Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation & Anr.
legal_issue: Whether compensation under the MV Act should be reduced by amounts the claimants receive from other sources (e.g. provident fund, insurance payouts).
holding_summary: Held such other receipts are generally not to be deducted from motor accident compensation, since the Act aims at just compensation for the specific wrong, independent of unrelated benefits.
principle_summary: Establishes the no deduction for collateral benefits principle in MACT compensation.

case_title: General Manager, Kerala State Road Transport Corporation v. Susamma Thomas & Ors.
legal_issue: Choice between the Davies and Nance methods for computing loss of dependency, and whether future prospects should be added to income.
holding_summary: Adopted the Davies (multiplier) method over the Nance method for India, and held future career prospects of a person with a stable job should be factored into the income used for computing dependency.
principle_summary: The foundational case that all later multiplier and future-prospects jurisprudence (Trilok Chandra, Sarla Verma, Pranay Sethi) builds on.

case_title: U.P. State Road Transport Corporation v. Trilok Chandra & Ors.
legal_issue: Whether an extremely high multiplier (approaching the deceaseds full remaining working life) is appropriate.
holding_summary: Held multipliers should not exceed a reasonable ceiling (around 16 in that case) even for young deceased victims, to avoid over-compensation from an unrealistically long multiplier.
principle_summary: An intermediate step between Susamma Thomas and the fixed age-band table later adopted in Sarla Verma.

case_title: [Case name and citation not confirmed] - Compensation appeal that expanded into a road-safety PIL challenging the 120 km/h speed-limit notification
legal_issue: Whether the Unions 6 April 2018 notification (S.O. 1522(E)) raising expressway/national-highway speed limits to 120 km/h was validly issued having regard to road-safety evidence.
holding_summary: A Division Bench (Justices N. Kirubakaran and T.V. Thamilselvi) quashed the notification as it applied within the cases scope and directed the Union and Tamil Nadu governments to issue fresh, evidence-based speed-limit notifications.
principle_summary: Real example of a source-level notification (SRC_SPEEDLIMIT_SO1522E_2018) being judicially invalidated in one jurisdiction while continuing to apply elsewhere - the exact scenario your effective_to/jurisdiction-override design needs to handle.
